summary: Yakima County tower built 1935 by CCC-ID crews and removed in 1965; none stand today, and the Yakama Nation requires permission to access the site.

facts.design: Three-legged wooden tower with an 8x8-foot cab and a ground house for living quarters
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1965; none remain standing per the register
facts.agency: Yakama Nation (the register calls it the Yakima Indian Reservation)

access.note: On the Yakama Nation; Willhite Web says access is forbidden without special permission

visit.trail_note: Permission from the Yakama Nation is required, and no tower stands

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give a 40-foot tower; Willhite Web gives 50 feet. The numeric height is left out of facts and the story reports both figures.

The register says Yakima Indian Reservation and Willhite Web says Yakama Nation. Both names describe the same reservation in Yakima County, so the record uses Yakama Nation and the story gives the register's name too.

notes_for_editor: Four short pages, no staffing, fire or site-today detail; the story says plainly that no source describes what remains. The 40 ft vs 50 ft height conflict is unresolved and kept out of the numeric height field. Access 'permission' matches the brief. Willhite Web's photo captions (McKays Butte in 1938, Yakaima Agency photo) have no image URLs, so no photos were added.
